title: Kernel grants large elimination to a Prop inductive through a dishonest autoParam, allowing an axiom-free proof of False
summary: The kernel's inductive checker strips `autoParam`/`optParam`/`outParam`/`semiOutParam` from binder domains by constant name alone, without checking how those constants are defined. `elim_only_at_universe_zero` also builds the constructor's parameters from the constructor's own (stripped) binder domains rather than from the header parameters that `check_constructors` uses. With a root-level `autoParam (A : Type) (B : Type 1) := B`, a constructor parameter `(p : autoParam Prop Type)` unfolds to `Type` for `check_constructors` but is stripped to `Prop` for the elimination check. A field `x : p` is then treated as a proof, so `P (p : Type) : Prop` gets a recursor into `Sort u`, and proof irrelevance gives a proof of False with no axioms. Reachable only through metaprogramming that sends declarations directly to the kernel, in an environment without Init's honest `autoParam` (built from `Init.Prelude`, or a `prelude` module).
